hardDay.heading: Hard day? Start here.
hardDay.body:
This chapter is conviction, not crushing. Jesus does not break a bruised reed. If you're sincerely stuck, you're not a project to fix. You're a child He's patient with.

Your task this week is honesty and one trusted believer. Read "A Pastoral Word to the Sincerely Stuck." If your fear feels bigger than a costume, like panic or dread, please talk with a pastor or counselor now.

If you are in danger, or you are having thoughts of not wanting to live, please stop here and reach out now. In the U.S., call or text 988, or call 911. Then tell a pastor or a trusted believer today.

bookRef.section: A Pastoral Word to the Sincerely Stuck

read.heading: Read first: Chapter 8
read.body:
Open to Chapter 8, "Fear Wearing Faith's Clothes." Read the opening story, then "How Fear Borrows Christian Vocabulary."

The opening is my story. I've always loved technology, and my wife saw a gift in me I wouldn't claim. My answer sounded spiritual. I told myself God hadn't called me to that. The real reason was smaller. I was afraid. I hadn't gone to school for it. That delay cost me. When I finally started, I didn't have a complete map. What I needed was the first step.

Then read the costume list. Fear borrows our church words. See which costume you've been wearing, and come back.

bookRef.section: Opening story; How Fear Borrows Christian Vocabulary

read.quote: Fear wore the clothes of calling, and I called the freeze faithfulness.
prompts: What gift has someone seen in me that I keep shelving with a holy-sounding reason?

pulse.heading: The pulse: two kinds of fear
pulse.body:
There are two kinds of fear. The fear of the Lord is reverence. It bows, listens, and obeys. Anxious fear refuses, and then it dresses up in religious language.

When Isaiah saw the Lord, he was undone, and then he said, "Here I am! Send me." Reverent fear and available obedience can live in the same heart.

verses.text: for God gave us a spirit not of fear but of power and love and self-control.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the Holy One is insight.
And I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here I am! Send me.”

prompts: Which kind of fear has been running my decisions lately?

nameIt.heading: Name it: the costume audit
nameIt.body:
Here are the costumes from Chapter 8: "I'm waiting on God." "I don't want to get ahead of God." "I'm surrendering the outcome." "It's a closed door." "I have a check in my spirit." Sometimes those are true. Sometimes they're fear in church clothes.

Under the costume, fear has a real name. Chapter 8 lists its faces: fear of failure, fear of people, fear of loss, fear of being seen, even fear of success. Name yours plainly.

bookRef.section: How Fear Borrows Christian Vocabulary; The Faces Fear Wears

verses.text: When I am afraid, I put my trust in you. In God, whose word I praise, in God I trust; I shall not be afraid. What can flesh do to me?
The fear of man lays a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is safe.
He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? Have you still no faith?”

prompts: Which costume fits me most right now?
What is my fear's real name under the religious phrase?
Would a wise believer say I'm waiting, or hiding?

build.heading: Build it: five concrete steps
build.body:
Chapter 8 gives five steps for when fear has learned church language:

Name the fear out loud before God. Bring it to Him with Scripture open. Separate holy waiting from clear duty. Take the clear duty already given. Invite one wise believer into the truth.

Work through them here. If there's no clear duty and wise counsel still says not yet, then wait with courage, not paralysis.

verses.text: Wait for the LORD; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the LORD!

prompts: The fear, named plainly:
Is there a clear duty already given? What is it?
I'll take it within 72 hours, by:
The wise believer I'll invite in:

move.heading: Move: this week's practice
move.body:
From the end of Chapter 8:

Pray the fear out loud without polishing it. Then take one clear duty already given, like a call, a confession, an application, or an act of service, within 72 hours.

The step doesn't have to be dramatic. It has to be obedient. If 72 hours pass, set a new time within three days.
prompts: I prayed the fear out loud, unpolished
I took one clear duty within 72 hours
Missed it? New time (within three days):
move.cta: Close the app and go take your step

help.heading: Help: waiting or hiding?
help.body:
Fear thrives in private. Bring one answer to a trusted believer this week, and ask them the question from the book about yourself: "Am I waiting, or am I hiding?" Pick someone who loves you enough to disagree with your delay.

If you want to help someone else, don't diagnose their fear. Tell them about the costume you took off, and ask how you can pray for them.
prompts: The believer I'll ask, "Am I waiting or hiding?":
Someone I'll pray for (first name or initials):
help.cta: Send it, then put the phone down

pray.heading: Pray it: unpolished
pray.body:
Don't clean this up. Pray it the way it really is.

God, here's the truth. I'm afraid of ____.

I've been calling it ____, but it's fear.

You say You are with me and You will hold me up. Your mercies are new this morning. You will never leave me. So I'm going to do ____ by ____, scared or not. Hold me up as I go. In Jesus' name, amen.

verses.text: fear not, for I am with you; be not dismayed, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my righteous right hand.
The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases; his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
Keep your life free from love of money, and be content with what you have, for he has said, “I will never leave you nor forsake you.”

prompts: What I'm afraid of:

review.heading: Review: name it, bring it, walk on
review.body:
After 72 hours, mark it: took the step, not yet, or holy wait.

Guardrail from Chapter 8: this isn't presumption, and it isn't hustle. Holy waiting is still real. And God's sovereignty is what lets you rest after you move.

If you're sincerely stuck, hear the gentleness here. A bruised reed He will not break. Name it, bring it, walk on.
